title: Signed reflection orbits from triangular group coordinates
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Groups are affine $F$-group schemes of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and subgroups are closed subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Smoothness and connectedness mean [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. Write $\mathbf G_a,\mathbf G_m$ for [def-sc-gm-ga]. Let $G$ be smooth and connected and $T\subseteq G$ a split maximal torus, that is, a subgroup isomorphic to $\mathbf G_m^r$ and maximal among such subgroups. Write $N_G(T)$ for the subgroup functor normalizing $T$ after every scalar extension. Put $X=\operatorname{Hom}(T,\mathbf G_m)$ and $Y=\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf G_m,T)$, paired by $\chi\circ\eta(t)=t^{\langle\chi,\eta\rangle}$. Let $D\subset X\setminus\{0\}$ be finite, nonempty and $\mathbf Z$-linearly independent. For a cocharacter $\eta$, let $U_G(\eta)$ be the subgroup functor of points $g$ for which $\eta(t)g\eta(t)^{-1}$ extends to $t=0$ with value $1$, and let $Z_G(\eta)$ be the subgroup functor centralizing $\eta(\mathbf G_m)$ after every scalar extension. Let $U,V\subseteq G$ be smooth connected unipotent subgroups normalized by $T$, where unipotent means that geometric points are unipotent matrices in a faithful representation. Suppose multiplication $V\times T\times U\to G$ is an open immersion, $Z_G(\lambda)=T$, $U_G(\lambda)=U$ and $U_G(-\lambda)=V$ for some $\lambda\in Y$ with $\langle\alpha,\lambda\rangle=n>0$ for all $\alpha\in D$. For each $\alpha$ suppose given $T$-normalized subgroups $U_\alpha\subset U$ and $V_\alpha\subset V$, with isomorphisms from $\mathbf G_a$ on which conjugation by $T$ scales the parameter by $\alpha$ and $-\alpha$, respectively. Suppose these subgroups generate $U$ and $V$ as closed subgroups. For each $\alpha$ let $n_\alpha\in N_G(T)(F)$ conjugate $U_\alpha$ onto $V_\alpha$ and act on $X$ by $s_\alpha(x)=x-\langle x,c_\alpha\rangle\alpha$, where $c_\alpha\in Y$ and $\langle\alpha,c_\alpha\rangle=2$. Assume that whenever $\eta\in Y$ has $\langle\beta,\eta\rangle\ge0$ for all $\beta\in D$, conjugation by $\eta$ extends to an action of the multiplicative monoid $\mathbf A^1$ on $U$. For each $\alpha$ choose $\eta_\alpha\in Y$ with $\langle\alpha,\eta_\alpha\rangle=0$ and $\langle\beta,\eta_\alpha\rangle=m_\alpha>0$ for every $\beta\ne\alpha$. Suppose evaluation at zero is a homomorphism $p_\alpha:U\to U_\alpha$ restricting to the identity on $U_\alpha$, with smooth connected kernel $K_\alpha$, $U=U_\alpha\ltimes K_\alpha$, $C_U(\eta_\alpha)=U_\alpha$, and $n_\alpha K_\alpha n_\alpha^{-1}=K_\alpha$. Let $W\subset\operatorname{Aut}(X)$ be generated by the $s_\alpha$ and put $R=\{w\alpha:w\in W,\alpha\in D\}$. Then $W$ is finite and $R$ is a reduced crystallographic root system in its rational span, with simple-root base $D$: every $\rho\in R$ has integral $D$-coefficients all nonnegative or all nonpositive. Here reduced crystallographic root system means a finite spanning set of nonzero vectors, with only $\rho,-\rho$ on each root line, stable under its root reflections with integral Cartan pairings; roots need not span $X\otimes\mathbf Q$. For each $\rho=w\alpha$, the conjugate $\dot wU_\alpha\dot w^{-1}$, for a word $\dot w$ in the $n_\beta^{\pm1}$ inducing $w$, depends only on $\rho$; call it $U_\rho$. It lies in $U$ or $V$ according as $\langle\rho,\lambda\rangle$ is positive or negative. There is a word $\dot w_0$ with $w_0D=-D$, $\dot w_0 U\dot w_0^{-1}=V$ and $\dot w_0 V\dot w_0^{-1}=U$. This assertion does not identify $R$ with all the adjoint weights of $G$ and assumes no reductivity of $G$.

source.place: Theorem 23.31 and Remark 23.33, p.494; normalizer finiteness in 17.19 and rank-one reflections in 21.11. Supporting assertion: reflection orbits, root signs and longest conjugation before reductivity (Steinberg 1999, 5.14--5.17).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-torus-normalizer-components] to the smooth connected affine finite-type group $G$ and its torus $T$. Conjugation on $X$ factors through the finite group $N_G(T)(F)/C_G(T)(F)$, since a centralizing element acts identically on $T$ and hence on every character. Each generator $s_\alpha$ is induced by the specified $n_\alpha$, so $W$ is a subgroup of this finite image and is finite. Consequently $R=WD$ is finite and contains no zero.

source.place: Corollaries 12.40 and 13.10--13.11, printed pp.244,257; no reductivity hypothesis.

proof.text: The split case of [lem-sfb-multiplicative-character-antiduality], with separable closure $F$ itself and $T\simeq\mathbf G_m^r=D_F(\mathbf Z^r)$, identifies $X$ with $\mathbf Z^r$ and $Y=\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf G_m,T)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf Z}(X,\mathbf Z)$, with the displayed composition pairing. Put $L=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in D}\mathbf Z\alpha$ and $E=L\otimes\mathbf Q$. The reflection formula shows $s_\alpha(L)\subseteq L$ and $s_\alpha^2=1$, so $W$ preserves $L$ bijectively. In particular $R\subset L$ and $\operatorname{span}_{\mathbf Q}R=E$. For each $\delta\in D$, extend the coefficient functional $\sum a_\beta\beta\mapsto a_\delta$ from $E$ to $X\otimes\mathbf Q$ by extending $D$ to a rational basis. Multiply this extended rational functional by a positive common denominator of its values on a basis of $X$. The resulting $\eta_\delta^*\in Y$ satisfies $\langle\delta,\eta_\delta^*\rangle=h_\delta>0$ and $\langle\beta,\eta_\delta^*\rangle=0$ for $\beta\ne\delta$.

source.place: Sections 12(a)--(c), especially Theorems 12.8--12.9, printed pp.230--234, split character antiduality; elementary lattice computations.

proof.text: For any word $\dot w$ inducing $w$ and any $\alpha\in D$, let $a:\mathbf G_a\hookrightarrow G$ parametrize $A=\dot wU_\alpha\dot w^{-1}$. It is a closed immersion and $T$ conjugates its parameter by $\rho=w\alpha$. Thus conjugation by a cocharacter $\nu$ is $a(z)\mapsto a(t^{\langle\rho,\nu\rangle}z)$ on every scalar algebra. If $\langle\rho,\lambda\rangle>0$ this formula extends at zero with value $1$, so $A\subset U_G(\lambda)=U$; if it is negative, $A\subset V$. It cannot be zero: then $A\subset Z_G(\lambda)=T$. In torus coordinates every morphism $\mathbf G_a\to T$ sends each invertible coordinate to a unit of $F[z]$, hence to a nonzero constant. A group morphism sends zero to $1$, so all these constants are $1$, contradicting the closed embedding of $\mathbf G_a$. Here the coordinate descriptions are [def-sc-gm-ga].

source.place: Theorem 23.31 and Remark 23.33, printed p.494: supporting triangular-coordinate assertion. Elementary argument from the stated hypotheses; Appendix C.1, C.8, C.12--C.14, C.19--C.22, printed pp.607--612.

proof.text: Suppose $\langle\rho,\lambda\rangle>0$, so the preceding closed additive line $A$ lies in $U$. If $\eta\in Y$ is nonnegative on $D$, let $b:\mathbf A^1\times U\to U$ be the hypothesized monoid action and put $k=\langle\rho,\eta\rangle$. As $A\hookrightarrow U$ is a closed immersion of affine schemes, its coordinate $z$ lifts to $f\in\mathcal O(U)$. Pulling $f$ back along $(t,z)\mapsto b(t,a(z))$ gives a polynomial $P(t,z)\in F[t,z]$ whose localization is $t^kz\in F[t,t^{-1},z]$. Negative $k$ is impossible by uniqueness of Laurent coefficients. Applying this to $\eta_\delta^*$ of step 2 gives $h_\delta a_\delta\ge0$ for every coefficient in $\rho=\sum a_\delta\delta$. Thus all $a_\delta\ge0$. If $\langle\rho,\lambda\rangle<0$, then $-\rho=w s_\alpha\alpha\in R$ and the argument applied to that word gives all coefficients of $\rho$ nonpositive. Step 3 excludes the remaining zero case. The polynomial/Laurent coordinates are [def-sc-gm-ga].

proof.text: Reducedness is a lattice calculation, independent of the signs. If $\rho=w\alpha$ and $\tau=v\beta$ lie on the same real root line, write $\tau=q\rho$ with $q\ne0$. Applying $w^{-1}$ gives $w^{-1}\tau=q\alpha\in L$, so the $D$-coordinate at $\alpha$ shows $q\in\mathbf Z$. Applying $v^{-1}$ to $\rho$ gives $v^{-1}\rho=q^{-1}\beta\in L$, so $q^{-1}\in\mathbf Z$. Therefore $q=\pm1$. Conversely $-\rho=w s_\alpha\alpha\in R$. Thus each root line meets $R$ precisely in $\rho,-\rho$.

source.place: Theorem 23.31 and Remark 23.33, printed p.494: supporting triangular-coordinate assertion. Elementary argument from the stated hypotheses; Appendix C.1, C.8, C.12--C.14, C.19--C.22, printed pp.607--612.

proof.text: On $E_{\mathbf R}=L\otimes\mathbf R$, take the Euclidean form $B_0$ for which $D$ is orthonormal and define $B(x,y)=\sum_{w\in W}B_0(wx,wy)$. It is symmetric and positive definite: every summand of $B(x,x)$ is nonnegative and the identity summand is positive for $x\ne0$. Reindexing the finite sum proves $W$-invariance. For $\rho=w\alpha$, put $r_\rho=w s_\alpha w^{-1}$ and $d_\rho(x)=\langle w^{-1}x,c_\alpha\rangle$. Then $r_\rho x=x-d_\rho(x)\rho$ and $r_\rho\rho=-\rho$. Orthogonality gives $B(r_\rho x,r_\rho\rho)=B(x,\rho)$, hence $d_\rho(x)=2B(x,\rho)/B(\rho,\rho)$. In particular $r_\rho$ and $d_\rho$ on $E$ depend only on $\rho$, not its expression as $w\alpha$.

source.place: Theorem 23.31 and Remark 23.33, printed p.494: supporting triangular-coordinate assertion. Elementary argument from the stated hypotheses; Appendix C.1, C.8, C.12--C.14, C.19--C.22, printed pp.607--612.

proof.text: The reflection $r_\rho\in W$ permutes $R$. For $\tau\in R\subset X$, its Cartan pairing is $d_\rho(\tau)=\langle w^{-1}\tau,c_\alpha\rangle\in\mathbf Z$; also $d_\rho(\rho)=2$. These formulas define rational functionals on $E$, since $d_\rho$ was obtained by extending an integral functional on $X$. Along with finiteness, spanning and nonvanishing in steps 1--2 and reducedness in step 5, these are precisely the root-system axioms in the statement. Finally $D$ is a rational basis of $E$ and step 4 supplies its signed integral expansions, so it is the asserted simple-root base. No assertion about other adjoint weights is used.

source.place: Theorem 23.31 and Remark 23.33, printed p.494: supporting triangular-coordinate assertion. Elementary argument from the stated hypotheses; Appendix C.1, C.8, C.12--C.14, C.19--C.22, printed pp.607--612.

proof.text: We first check uniqueness for a simple character $\alpha$. Any $T$-equivariant closed embedding $a:\mathbf G_a\hookrightarrow G$ with character $\alpha$ lies in $U$ by the same parameter calculation as step 3. Since $\langle\alpha,\eta_\alpha\rangle=0$, its image lies scheme-theoretically in $C_U(\eta_\alpha)=U_\alpha$. This resulting closed immersion $\mathbf G_a\hookrightarrow U_\alpha\simeq\mathbf G_a$ has surjective coordinate map $F[x]\to F[z]$, $x\mapsto P(z)$, by [def-sc-gm-ga]. Surjectivity gives a polynomial $Q$ with $Q(P(z))=z$, so both $P$ and $Q$ have degree one; the identity condition gives $P(0)=0$. Thus it is an isomorphism onto $U_\alpha$. Now if two conjugates have character $\rho=w\alpha=v\beta$, conjugating both by $\dot w^{-1}$ gives closed additive lines of character $\alpha$, so both equal $U_\alpha$ by the preceding calculation. Conjugating back proves independence of the word and of the chosen simple root. Step 3 gives the claimed location in $U$ or $V$.

source.place: Theorem 23.31 and Remark 23.33, printed p.494: supporting triangular-coordinate assertion. Elementary argument from the stated hypotheses; Appendix C.1, C.8, C.12--C.14, C.19--C.22, printed pp.607--612.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-root-chamber-simple-transitivity] to $(E_{\mathbf R},B,R,D)$: steps 1--7 verified finiteness, spanning, reducedness, orthogonal root reflections, integral Cartan pairings, and the signed basis, exactly its hypotheses. The root reflection group there equals the image of $W$ on $E_{\mathbf R}$: every simple reflection is a root reflection, and every root reflection is $w s_\alpha w^{-1}$. Both $D$ and $-D$ are bases. Transitivity gives an element sending $C_D$ to $C_{-D}$; equivariance and injectivity of the base/chamber bijection give $w_0D=-D$. Lift it to a word $\dot w_0$ in the specified $n_\alpha^{\pm1}$.

source.place: Appendix C.9--C.10, printed pp.609--610, and C.19--C.22, printed pp.611--612; apply only after constructing the reduced root system.

proof.text: For $\beta\in D$, $V_\beta=n_\beta U_\beta n_\beta^{-1}$ has character $-\beta$. If $w_0\alpha=-\beta$, step 8 identifies $\dot w_0U_\alpha\dot w_0^{-1}$ with $V_\beta$. Since $w_0$ bijects $D$ onto $-D$ and the $U_\alpha$, respectively $V_\beta$, generate $U$, respectively $V$, conjugation carries the smallest closed subgroup containing the first family onto that containing the second. Hence $\dot w_0U\dot w_0^{-1}=V$. Also $w_0(-D)=D$; applying step 8 to $\dot w_0V_\alpha\dot w_0^{-1}$ gives the corresponding $U_\beta$, so $\dot w_0V\dot w_0^{-1}=U$ by the same generation argument.

Step 1: torus-normalizer-components (smooth connected G, any torus, no reductivity) gives a finite N(F)/C(F), so W is finite. Step 2: split antiduality identifies Y with Hom(X,Z); s_alpha preserves L and squares to 1; clearing denominators gives eta*_delta. Step 3: the conjugate by a word has character w·alpha (left action); a positive or negative pairing with lambda puts it in U or V; a zero pairing would make it lie in T and be trivial. Step 4: the f in F[t,z] versus Laurent t^k z argument gives k>=0, hence signed coefficients. Step 5: q and 1/q integral in the D-lattice gives reducedness, including for non-primitive alpha in X. Step 6: the averaged form gives d_rho=2B(x,rho)/B(rho,rho). Step 7: Cartan numbers are integral, so all root-system axioms hold. Step 8: C_U(eta_alpha)=U_alpha plus the degree-one argument for a closed immersion G_a->G_a gives uniqueness of U_rho. Step 9: the hypotheses of root-chamber-simple-transitivity hold; the image of W equals W_R, so w_0 D=-D. Step 10: the generation argument gives both U->V and V->U. Edge cases: rank one, central torus directions, characteristic p. Unused hypotheses (open cell, p_alpha, K_alpha) are harmless. All theorem cites are in the item's own unit, so no tool_uses.
